title: Codebase and task skills with evals
bridge: A codebase skill is like the onboarding doc you wished for on day one: where things live, and where it hurts. Except: an agent reads it, and only when the task touches that code. So it stays short, points to deeper guides, and has eval cases that prove it changes what the agent does.
intro: With the marketplace, CI and the core skills in place, the guilds write the skills routines will lean on. Three codebase skills (frontend, backend, DevOps) give the map. Task skills (fix a bug, fix CI, fix a flaky test, and five more) give the method. Every skill ships with 3 to 10 eval cases, and this lesson reads two of them line by line.

picture.caption: A task loads the right skills; eval cases prove each skill fires when it should and stays quiet when it should not.

a skill that does not beat no-skill gets trimmed or rewritten

p: The FE guild writes fe-codebase in the fe-guild plugin. Start from frontend/AGENTS.md and the reviewer memory in pr-code-review/references/memory (25 files), and link to them instead of copying. Add the guild's own review habits: tests through Storybook stories, not class names; useQuery over useResult.

Its eval cases are case.yaml files with graders. It fires for a frontend task, and a component change gets a story per state. A new e2e flow goes into e2e/pages/*Page.ts with Given/When/Then steps. It stays quiet for a backend task. Run claude plugin eval plugins/fe-guild locally before the PR; the owner is the FE guild.
sections.because: We add a paths field, because the skill should load for work under frontend/ and nowhere else.

code.text:
---
name: fe-codebase
description: "Use when working in fcp/frontend: where things live, the design system, data fetching with useQuery, layouts that work from 760 to 1440 px with container queries, Storybook stories per state, e2e page objects with test.step, and the risky areas."
when_to_use: "Any edit, review or plan that touches frontend/ (components, pages, hooks, e2e specs, stories)."
paths: ["frontend/**"]
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# fe-codebase

Goal: a change that looks and works right from 760 to 1440 px, matches the design system, and is proven by tests
that read what the user sees.

## Where things live
- `src/components/designSystem/` holds shared UI and `src/components/app/` app-specific parts. Reuse before you build.
- `e2e/pages/*Page.ts` page objects own selectors and flows; specs in `e2e/pr/` only orchestrate, in Given/When/Then steps.
- Unit tests live in `test/unit/` (Vitest, happy-dom); `@r` points at `src/`.

## Signs to look deeper
- A table or form that also lives in a slide-in panel: use `@container` with `@md:`/`@lg:`, not window breakpoints.
- A new data fetch: useQuery, not useResult; check the loading, empty and error states.
- A test that finds elements by class name: use test IDs, ARIA roles or visible text, or a Storybook story per state.
- Code near the RSC boundary, dates and time zones, or global CSS: read references/risky-areas.md.

Run `npm run verify` before you say done (verify skill).

sections.h: be-codebase and its eval case, part 1 (G8-11)
p: be-codebase is the BE guild's short entry point over the moved be-module-* skills. It says what matters and sends the agent to be-module-cloud, be-module-client or be-module-sdk for depth, so those load only when needed. Signs to look deeper: a migration on a big table, a proto change, a serializer the SDK uses. Also a Celery task signature, a permission check, or the client's raw (PHI) database.

The ticket's sketch is an eval case, not the skill. An eval case is a folder with a case.yaml (lesson p12-3). It holds a prompt, the tools the agent may use, optional context, and graders that score the answer.
sections.because: We give the case a trimmed fixture, because it must run anywhere and hold no customer data.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/plugins/be-guild/evals/be-codebase/proto-change/case.yaml
schema_version: "1.1"
name: be-codebase-proto-change
tags: [nightly, be-codebase] # has an llm grader, so it runs nightly, not on every PR
execution:
  prompt: >
    In fcp I need the on-prem client to send the cloud a new "disk_free_bytes" value with its heartbeat.
    The messages are in common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc. Tell me what to change and what to watch out for.
  allowed_tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]
  max_turns: 200 # the eval tool's ceiling; a turn cap shouldn't decide the score
  timeout_seconds: 3600
context:
  add_dirs: [fixture] # a trimmed copy of the protos and handlers; no customer data

notes.text: Where the case lives: evals/<skill>/<case>/case.yaml.
The case file format version.
A unique case name.
It has an LLM grader, so it runs nightly, not on every PR.
What the agent is asked and allowed.
A real-looking request: a new heartbeat value from client to cloud.
Read-only tools plus Skill, so the agent can load skills.
The eval tool's ceiling, set high so a turn cap never decides the score.
The tool's wall-clock ceiling for one run, also set far away.
A trimmed copy of the protos and handlers; no customer data.

callout.text: max_turns: 200 and timeout_seconds: 3600 are settings of the eval runner for one test case, not limits on an agent. The tool's defaults (10 turns, 300 seconds) would fail a good answer that needs more steps, so we raise them. Agents in production still run with no turn or time limit.

sections.h: be-codebase's eval case, part 2: three graders
p: A grader scores one property of the run. tool_used checks which tools were called and with what input. regex looks for a pattern in the answer. llm asks a judge model with written criteria; it costs model calls, so cases with one are tagged nightly.
sections.because: We mix a free check that the skill fired with a judge, because firing alone does not prove the answer right.

code.text:
graders:
  - name: skill-fired
    type: tool_used
    tool: Skill
    input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?be-codebase"'
  - name: names-protoc
    type: regex
    pattern: "make protoc"
  - name: back-compat
    type: llm
    criteria: >
      PASS if the answer adds a new field instead of changing existing ones, says clients already installed at
      customers must keep working, and says to regenerate and commit the _pb2 files. FAIL if it renames or removes a field.

notes.text: The scoring rules.
Grader 1: did the agent load be-codebase?
Look at tool calls ...
... to the Skill tool ...
... whose input names be-codebase, with or without the be-guild: prefix.
Grader 2: does the answer mention make protoc?
A plain regex on the answer.
Grader 3: the judge.
PASS for a new field, old clients kept working and regenerated _pb2 files; FAIL for a renamed or removed field.

callout.text: More be-codebase cases: a model change mentions makemigrations --check and lock risk. A serializer change checks SDK use. It stays quiet on a frontend task. Cases tagged pr use only free graders. Grader patterns are JavaScript regular expressions, so Python's inline (?i) throws an error (lesson p12-3).

p: DevOps writes two skills in devops-guild. devops-codebase is the map. It covers the old multi_tenant/ tree (root.hcl), the new terraform/ tree for accounts such as ai-agents, and module refs. It adds the n8n pattern for inf tools, gitops' argocd-apps chart, Vault paths and naming (ai-agents for AI, rhino-agent for client VMs). infra-change is the habit, shown below.

Eval cases: a VPC change gets a blast-radius note. A request to apply right away is declined with the safe path. A values change names the environments it hits, and the skill stays quiet for a frontend task.
sections.because: We explain the safe path, because the walls are enforced elsewhere and the agent needs to know what to do instead.

code.text:
---
name: infra-change
description: "Use for any change in the infrastructure or gitops repos or in workflow files: the checks to run without cloud keys, how to get a plan, and the blast-radius and rollback notes every infra PR needs. A person applies; agents never apply, destroy or sync."
when_to_use: "Editing terragrunt.hcl, modules/, Helm values, Argo CD apps, Packer images or .github/workflows; asked to 'deploy', 'apply' or 'roll out'."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# infra-change

Goal: a reviewer can see what this changes, where, and how to undo it, before anyone applies it.

## Checks that need no cloud keys
`tofu fmt -check -recursive`, `terragrunt hcl format --check`, `terragrunt validate` on the units you touched, then
tflint, `trivy config .` and checkov. For gitops: `helm lint` and `helm template | kubeconform`. For workflows:
actionlint and zizmor.

## The plan
The plan comes from CI with a read-only role, or a person runs it over VPN and pastes it into the PR. You don't run
apply, destroy, argocd sync or workflow_dispatch; if the task seems to need one, stop and hand it to DevOps with
what you found.

## In every PR
- Blast radius: which accounts, clusters and environments change, and whether anything is replaced or deleted.
- Rollback: the revert, and what a revert doesn't undo (data, DNS, IAM).
- Look deeper when the plan shows a destroy or replace, IAM or security groups, state moves, or the shared inf cluster.

p: The bug fixers are the most important routines, and people follow the same steps. G8-18 writes three task skills. fix-bug and fix-ci go in rhino-core (owners: FE and BE guilds, Platform); fix-flaky-test goes in be-guild. The result checks (no skipped or deleted tests) are enforced elsewhere; these skills teach the method.

fix-ci asks whether main is red too, fingerprints the failure, and sorts it: code, test, environment or flaky. It makes the smallest fix and hands environment problems to DevOps. fix-flaky-test reproduces with repeats, random order, fixed seeds and parallel runs. It checks the usual causes: timing, shared state, order, time zones, network. It fixes the cause, never with retries or sleeps, and wants about 50 green runs.
sections.because: We make reproduction step 2, because a fix without a failing reproduction cannot show it fixed anything.

code.text:
---
name: fix-bug
description: "Use when the task is a reported bug: triage it, reproduce it first with a failing test or a recorded browser run on seed data, find the root cause with file:line, make the smallest safe fix, add a regression test, and look for the same pattern nearby."
when_to_use: "A Jira Bug ticket, a bug report in Slack, 'this is broken', 'X shows the wrong value'."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# fix-bug

Goal: a fix for the cause, not the symptom, proven by a test that failed before and passes after.

1. Triage: is it a duplicate (search Jira), which team owns it, how bad is it for users?
2. Reproduce first, at the level the user sees it: an API test for BE, a component or Playwright test for FE, or a
   recorded browser run on seed data in FCP Lab. Keep the reproduction.
3. If it won't reproduce, stop and report what you tried, on which data and commit, and ask the reporter one
   specific question. That report is useful on its own.
4. Root cause: name the file:line and why it happened (the wrong assumption, not only the line).
5. The smallest safe fix: the reproduction now passes and the rest of verify stays green.
6. Look nearby: the same pattern elsewhere? List the places in the PR; fix them only if the ticket covers them.

sections.h: The other task skills and a negative case (G8-19)
p: Five more task skills come from the guilds, each short with 3 to 10 eval cases. upgrade-dependency reads the changelog first, searches our usage and moves one package at a time. remove-dead-code takes candidates from knip (FE) or vulture (BE), proves each unused, and deletes in small batches. add-tests covers untested behaviour and plants a bug per test. merge-duplicates checks real duplication, and small-feature cuts reviewable slices.

DevOps writes security-fix with Ronen. It asks whether the finding is reachable and a fixed version is out. It covers the upgrade path, base-image rebuilds, the scanner before and after, and a link to the finding. Every skill gets at least one negative case: an unrelated request must not load it.
sections.because: We write a negative case for every skill, because a skill that loads on everything adds noise to every task.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/plugins/rhino-core/evals/remove-dead-code/stays-quiet-on-feature/case.yaml
schema_version: "1.1"
name: remove-dead-code-stays-quiet-on-feature
description: An unrelated feature request must not load remove-dead-code.
tags: [pr, remove-dead-code] # free graders only, so it runs on every PR
execution:
  prompt: "Add a 'Last updated' column to the datasets table in the dashboard, newest first."
  allowed_tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]
  max_turns: 200 # the eval tool's ceiling
graders:
  - name: does-not-fire
    type: tool_used
    tool: Skill
    input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?remove-dead-code"'
    min: 0
    max: 0
    arm: both # score it in both arms; a Skill grader is otherwise only an indicator

notes.text: The case's path.
A name that says what it checks.
The rule in plain words.
Free graders only, so it runs on every PR.
A feature request that has nothing to do with dead code.
Read-only tools plus Skill.
The eval tool's ceiling, as before.
The only grader.
Look at Skill calls ...
... that name remove-dead-code.
Zero calls allowed at least ...
... and at most: it must not fire.
Score it with and without the plugin; a Skill grader is otherwise only an indicator.

sections.h: Running a suite locally before the PR
p: claude plugin eval plugins/<plugin> runs the plugin's cases on your machine, as you, with a no-plugin baseline arm by default. --case <glob> picks cases, --tag picks tags, --runs sets runs per case (default 3), and --json writes the full result. Each run is a full Claude session on your own login, so start with one case and --runs 1.

Read the report the way CI does (lesson g8-3). Every case must reach the threshold, and none may be worse with the plugin. A skill that does not beat no-skill is trimmed or rewritten in the next rule diet.

quiz.q: Why does the be-codebase proto case carry the nightly tag instead of pr?

options.why: Speed is not the rule; graders are.

options.text: Because it has an LLM grader, and PR runs use free graders only.
options.why: A judge model costs calls, so those cases run nightly.

options.text: Because proto changes happen only at night.
options.why: The tag is about the case's graders, not when protos change.

quiz.q: What does a negative eval case such as stays-quiet-on-feature prove?

options.text: That the skill does not load for an unrelated request.
options.why: min 0 and max 0 on the Skill call: it must not fire.

options.text: That the skill produces no errors.
That the feature request is done correctly.
options.why: The case has no grader for the feature itself.

quiz.q: A routine is asked to "apply the VPC change, it's urgent". What does infra-change tell it?

options.text: Apply it, since a person asked.
options.why: Agents never apply, destroy or sync, whoever asks.

options.text: Run terragrunt apply with -lock=false so it does not block others.
options.why: No apply at all; -lock=false is only for read-only plans.

options.text: Decline, run the keyless checks, get a plan from CI, write blast radius and rollback, and hand it to DevOps.
options.why: That is the safe path the skill teaches; a person applies.
